# Teacher checkpoints — separate, not access-protected
Caesar output: Phhw dw 3, Urrp E!; inverse shift -3 restores text. 26 candidates include the original, but code does not automatically identify the intended plaintext. Non-ASCII characters and punctuation are preserved by the defined model. Historical cipher demonstrations are not secure encryption.
Identical UTF-8 inputs give identical fingerprints; supplied edits give different ones. Collision resistance is not mathematical impossibility of collisions. A replaced file/digest pair is not authenticated. No password-storage claim.
C1 passes supplied facts only. C2 fails hostname; C3 expired; C4 chain not trusted; C5 fails handshake possession proof; C6 fails permitted server use. All cards assume status handled and signatures checked unless explicitly failed; actual client behaviour needs real evidence.
TLS cards: T1,T2,T3,T4,T5. Hello shares -> secret derivation -> protected server authentication -> validation/Finished -> application records. Flow omits optional features and early data. Never say RSA transports a session key in TLS 1.3.
Encrypt to recipient public key/decrypt with recipient private key; sign with signer private key/verify with signer public key. Symmetric protected records use derived secret key material. Certificate issuer signature binds public information; server proves corresponding private-key possession during handshake.
Accept justified risk/control alternatives. HTTPS does not repair infected endpoints, excessive export privileges, disclosure through an authorised export or absent at-rest protection. Passing paper cards does not prove real TLS deployment.
